title: Index Maintenance Overhead
description: Understand write amplification, fragmentation, and index rebuild strategies

data.text: Every index adds maintenance cost during writes. Understanding fragmentation, page splits, and rebuild strategies helps maintain performance without accumulating unused indexes.

data.title: Cost components
items: INSERT: write to table and all indexes
UPDATE: modify table and affected indexes
DELETE: mark rows and clean indexes

data.title: Rebuild and reorganize
data.content: Use database-specific commands to reduce fragmentation.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Monitor index usage with DMVs or system views. Drop indexes with zero reads to reduce maintenance burden.

items.question: How often should I rebuild indexes?
items.answer: Depends on fragmentation. Rebuild when fragmentation exceeds 20-30 percent for large tables.

items.question: Does index maintenance slow production?
items.answer: Online or concurrent rebuilds minimize impact. Schedule heavy maintenance during low-traffic windows.

items.question: Should I index foreign keys?
items.answer: Yes. Unindexed foreign keys slow deletes and joins. Verify with database recommendations.

data.title: Summary
points: Indexes slow writes proportionally to their count
Drop unused indexes to reduce overhead
Rebuild or reorganize based on fragmentation thresholds
data.takeaway: Index maintenance is ongoing. Treat indexes as living objects that need monitoring, tuning, and cleanup.
